title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: G is a form of GL(2) over a base, namely the units of an Azumaya algebra M of rank 4. σ is a section of M with det σ (the reduced norm) invertible. SG is the subgroup of elements of reduced norm 1. Define the scheme A_σ = { y ∈ SG : Tr(yσ) = Tr σ }, with Tr the reduced trace.

The lemma states that the following conditions are equivalent:
- a) A_σ is stable under the translations y ↦ εy for ε ∈ μ_2 ⊂ G_m.
- b) Tr σ = 0.
- c) In the normal form of the earlier section IV (p. 452, normalisations (34), (38)), σ = (0 −1; −ν 0), i.e. the parameter w equals 1, i.e. ρ = (0 1; ν 1).
- d) σ² ∈ Γ(G_m), i.e. the image σ̃ of σ in PG is an involution (σ̃² = 1). b) implies d), and the converse holds when σ is nowhere scalar (this is completed on the next page).

Proofs:
- a) ⇔ b): if y ∈ A_σ then εy has determinant ε² = 1 and Tr(εyσ) = ε Tr σ. So stability amounts to ε Tr σ = Tr σ for all ε ∈ μ_2, i.e. Tr σ is a fixed point of μ_2 acting on the affine line E¹. Grothendieck phrases this as (E¹)^{μ_2} = 0, which holds functorially in any characteristic, since ε and 1 are independent in the coordinate ring of μ_2.
- b) ⇔ d): by Cayley–Hamilton, σ² − (Tr σ)σ + det σ = 0.

The purpose is to prepare the analysis of the twisted 'loop equation' ξ = η ε(μ−1) of the previous page, where η = ε[β,σ]. To reduce to case (II), one needs Tr η = Tr σ, i.e. ε Tr σ = Tr σ. The lemma isolates the case Tr σ = 0, where the ε-twisted equation has a μ_2-symmetry. The next page then defines the solution scheme G*_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G×G×E'×E' with a morphism ε to μ_2.

The normal form (σ of trace 0, ρ of trace 1) mirrors the order-2 / order-3 generators of PSL_2(Z) used in Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type relations. Here they are deformed to 2-dimensional forms of GL(2).
errors: On the next page, 'Tr σ = 0 ⇒ σ = det σ·1' is a slip: Cayley–Hamilton gives σ² = −det σ·1.
a) ⇒ b) tacitly requires A_σ to have enough points (e.g. to be fpqc-surjective over the base); otherwise stability is vacuous on empty fibres.
b) ⇐ d) needs σ to be non-scalar in every fibre; Grothendieck notes this hypothesis only on the next page.

ideas.what: Equivalence of the μ_2-invariance of the slice {det y = 1, Tr(yσ) = Tr σ} with Tr σ = 0 and with σ being an involution in PG
ideas.modern_name: Trace-zero elements of a quaternion/Azumaya algebra; involutions in PGL_2 via Cayley–Hamilton

ideas.what: Normal form of the pair (ρ, σ) in a form of GL(2), with σ of trace 0 and ρ of trace 1, as deformed images of the modular-group generators in the study of the 'équation des lacets'
ideas.modern_name: 2-dimensional (twisted) representations / solution schemes of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's unpublished program; GT theory more generally Drinfeld, Ihara
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to remarks in La Longue Marche (1981); unsure

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary lemma (Cayley–Hamilton, μ_2-fixed points) serving a larger unpublished computation of loop-equation solutions in forms of GL(2). It is not new in itself.

In (6) the first matrix has ν' in the lower-left, with ν' = −ν.
'E^{1 μ_2} = (0)' should be read as the μ_2-fixed subscheme of the affine line E¹ being zero.
